LanguageData.XTS_FilterArchiteDesc: Preset xenotypes containing archite genes (e.g., Sanguophage). Scenario xenotypes are grouped under the scenario row instead.
LanguageData.XTS_FilterInheritableDesc: Preset xenotypes whose xenogerm rewrites the pawn's germline: inheritable xenotypes (e.g., Impid, Yttakin) and Baseliner, whose empty xenogerm converts the pawn back to a baseliner.
LanguageData.XTS_FilterPlayerScenarioDesc: The custom xenotypes your scenario's starting colonists were created with. Xenotypes assembled in-game are never sold.
LanguageData.XTS_CustomXenotypeDesc: A custom xenotype your scenario's starting colonists were created with.
LanguageData.XTS_PricingSectionDesc: Market value formula for trader-sold xenogerms. Affects new xenogerms only.
LanguageData.XTS_BasePresetValueDesc: Base silver value added to all preset xenotype xenogerms
LanguageData.XTS_ValuePerMetabolismDesc: Silver value added per point of absolute metabolism
LanguageData.XTS_ValuePerComplexityDesc: Silver value added per point of genetic complexity
LanguageData.XTS_ValuePerArchiteDesc: Silver value added per archite gene
LanguageData.XTS_QuantitySectionDesc: How many xenogerms each trader kind carries, rolled from its range on every visit. Affects new traders only.
LanguageData.XTS_TraderCountDesc: Xenogerms this trader arrives with, rolled from this range each visit
LanguageData.XTS_ImplantationSectionDesc: How trader-sold xenogerms behave when implanted.
LanguageData.XTS_PreserveDeathrestCapacityDesc: Vanilla recreates the deathrest gene on every xenogerm implant or sanguophage reimplant, resetting serum-bought deathrest capacity to one. With this on, the pawn's previous capacity is restored whenever it still has a deathrest gene afterwards. Applies to all xenogerms, not just trader-sold ones.
LanguageData.XTS_ImplantGermlineAsEndogenesDesc: When a trader-sold xenogerm for a germline xenotype is implanted, its genes replace the pawn's endogenes instead of becoming xenogenes, making the pawn a born member of that xenotype: children inherit the genes, and later xenogerm implants add to them instead of overwriting them. Xenogenes the pawn already carries are kept, and a pawn named for them (a sanguophage, say) keeps its name and icon.
LanguageData.XTS_CommonalitySectionDesc: How a trader picks which xenotypes to stock, weighted by the prices of everything currently sellable. Affects new stock only.
LanguageData.XTS_StrategyInversePriceDesc: Cheaper xenogerms are more common: chance is proportional to 1 / price. Archite xenogerms stay rare.
LanguageData.XTS_StrategySoftInversePriceDesc: Cheaper xenogerms are more common, with a gentler bias: chance is proportional to 1 / √price.
LanguageData.XTS_StrategyPriceDesc: Pricier xenogerms are more common: chance is proportional to price.
LanguageData.XTS_StrategySqrtPriceDesc: Pricier xenogerms are more common, with a gentler bias: chance is proportional to √price.
LanguageData.XTS_StrategyBellCurveDesc: Mid-priced xenogerms are most common: chances follow a bell curve centred on the median price, so the cheapest and priciest are both rare.
LanguageData.XTS_StrategyUniformDesc: Every sellable xenotype is equally likely, regardless of price.
